To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we measured the production rates of 194 Hm, 207Bi, and 202Pb in Pb due to high energy neutrons.
we have measured the production of 207 Bi,  202 Pb, and 194 Hg due to high-energy cosmic neutrons in a sample of Pb using a neutron beam from the Los Alamos National Laboratory.
we measured the production rate of 194 H g, 202 Pb and 207 Bi in natural Pb due to cosmic neutron interactions at sea level.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the production rate of long-lived cosmogenically produced radionuclides in natural Pb, which is important for understanding potential backgrounds in Pb shielding in low background experiments.
the measurement of the production rate of long-lived nuclids in natural lead due to fast-neutron interactions.
the study of neutron-induced reactions of long-lived radionuclides that are produced from cosmic-ray spallation of natural lead.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the production rates of 207 Bi,  194 Hg and  202 Pb from cosmic rays in natural Pb are 8.0, 120, and 207 atoms per kilogram per day, respectively, at sea level.
these production rates are not a significant background for the proposed LUX experiment.
the production rate of long-lived nuclids due to cosmic neutrons in Pb is negligible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have measured a production rate of 207 Bi, which is the most abundant cosmogenic nuclide in natural Pb, and have measured the production rates of 194 Hm and 202 Pb for the first time.
the production of 207 Bi is negligible in the Pb shielding, but the production of 202 Pb is significant.
the production of 194 Hm, 202 Pb and 207 Bi are negligible compared to the production of 138 La.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production rates of these nuclides are not negligible, but are not a significant concern for low background experiments using large Pb shielding.
207 Bi and 202 Pb are produced in natural Pb at a rate comparable to the production of 210 Pb from 222 Rn.
the production rate of 194 H g from cosmic rays is much larger than the decay rate of 194 Au, which is the main source of the 194 Hg background for the LHC.
